CourseName: CEN3722 - Introduction to Human Computer Interfaces

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: A structured outline of the module's subject matter, covering task analysis fundamentals, Hierarchical Task Analysis (HTA), Cognitive Task Analysis (CTA), and method selection; used as the authoritative content map for building other module materials.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: This module overview page lists and briefly defines the core topics covered in Module 4, including foundational task analysis concepts, methods for breaking down user behaviors, and their application to interface design, serving as a navigation guide for learners to identify and access each subject area within the module.

Artifacts.Name: Module Outcomes
Artifacts.Description: A list of five measurable module outcomes spanning remembering HTA and CTA steps through applying, analyzing, and evaluating task analysis in interface design contexts, mapped to Bloom's levels and course objectives; used by instructors to align assessments and by learners to understand expected competencies.

Artifacts.Name: Task Analysis for AI-Assisted Software Design
Artifacts.Description: A group project assignment (Phase 3 of a semester-long sequence) in which student teams conduct a task analysis of an AI-assisted software design workflow, producing HTA diagrams and CTA findings that build on prior use-case work; used by student teams as the primary instructions for completing and submitting this phase.

Artifacts.Name: Foundations of Task Analysis
Artifacts.Description: A reading that introduces task analysis as a core UX and interface design practice, explaining what it is, why it matters, and how breaking down human activity into constituent parts helps designers build systems that support real-world user behavior.

Artifacts.Name: Hierarchical Task Analysis (HTA)
Artifacts.Description: A reading covering Hierarchical Task Analysis (HTA), tracing its origins in industrial and military psychology and explaining how the method decomposes complex user goals into progressively smaller sub-tasks, which learners use to understand and document observable task structures.

Artifacts.Name: Cognitive Task Analysis (CTA)
Artifacts.Description: A reading on Cognitive Task Analysis (CTA) that addresses the mental processes underlying user actions — such as expert decision-making and knowledge application — filling the gap that HTA leaves by going beyond observable steps to capture what users think and know during task execution.

Artifacts.Name: Comparing and Selecting Analysis Methods
Artifacts.Description: A reading that compares HTA and CTA as complementary rather than competing methods, guiding learners and instructors in selecting the appropriate analysis technique based on project context, task complexity, and the type of information needed.

Artifacts.Name: Data Collection for Task Analysis
Artifacts.Description: A reading on empirical data-collection techniques used to feed task analysis, covering methods such as observation and interviews, and explaining how to gather reliable, real-world evidence about how users actually perform tasks before analysis begins.

Artifacts.Name: Producing Task Analysis Documentation
Artifacts.Description: A reading explaining how to translate raw observational and interview data into structured, team-readable task analysis documents, covering documentation formats, verification practices, and how to produce artefacts that are ready to inform design decisions.

Artifacts.Name: Applying Task Analysis to the Group Project
Artifacts.Description: A reading that guides student project teams through applying task analysis collaboratively, addressing the practical challenges of coordinating multiple observers, aligning findings, and converting team-gathered evidence into structured, evidence-based design understanding.
